stem:
Zaid has quadrilateral ABCD in which ∠A = ∠B = ∠C = ∠D = 90°.

Can he classify ABCD as a rectangle without separately checking that opposite sides are equal?

options.text: He should call the figure a right angle, not a rectangle.
Yes, even if A, B, C, D were only three rays and not a closed quadrilateral.
Yes: a quadrilateral with all angles 90° is a rectangle; opposite-side equalities then follow.
The same rule also classifies any open broken line of four right turns as a rectangle.

teacher.key_rationale: A rectangle is a quadrilateral with all angles 90°; opposite sides then follow from congruent triangles. Renaming it a right angle, dropping the quadrilateral condition, or extending the rule to open paths all misuse the classification.
